qa.e: 'If and only if' joins a statement with its converse when both are true.

qa.q: 'If n is odd, then n² is odd' is true. Is its converse 'If n² is odd, then n is odd' true?
qa.a: Yes: if n were even, n² would be even, so n must be odd
qa.e: If n were even, n² = n × n would be even. So whenever n² is odd, n must be odd. Both directions are true.

qa.q: In △PQR, ∠Q = ∠R = 65° and PQ = 9 cm. What is PR?
qa.e: Sides opposite equal angles are equal: PR (opposite ∠Q) = PQ (opposite ∠R).

qa.q: To prove 'equal angles ⇒ equal opposite sides' in △ABC with ∠B = ∠C, which line is drawn?
qa.a: The altitude AD from A to BC
qa.e: The altitude gives two right triangles that can be shown congruent.

qa.q: In that proof, △ABD ≅ △ACD by which rule?
qa.e: ∠B = ∠C, ∠ADB = ∠ADC = 90°, and side AD is common.

qa.q: Which pair of triangles shows that equal area does not imply congruence?
qa.e: Both have area 15 but different bases, so they cannot be congruent.

qa.q: A triangle has sides 20, 21 and 29. Is it right-angled?
In the proof of the Pythagoras converse, why are the original triangle and the constructed right triangle congruent?
qa.a: SSS: a, b equal by construction and both third sides equal c
qa.e: The constructed hypotenuse is √(a² + b²) = c, so all three sides match.

qa.q: Which statement is the converse of 'If a triangle is right-angled with hypotenuse c, then a² + b² = c²'?
qa.a: If a² + b² = c², then the triangle is right-angled with hypotenuse c
qa.e: The converse swaps hypotenuse-condition and equation.

qa.q: A triangle has sides 7, 8 and 11. What can you say?
qa.e: The squares of the two smaller sides must add to the square of the largest.

qa.q: How many factors does 49 have?
qa.e: 1, 7, 49: the square of the prime 7.

qa.q: Which number has an odd number of factors?
qa.e: 64 = 8² is a perfect square, so its factor 8 pairs with itself.

qa.q: 'If a number is a multiple of 3, then it is even.' Which number is a counterexample?
qa.e: 9 is a multiple of 3 but odd.

qa.q: The converse 'If a number is even, then it is a multiple of 3' is:
qa.e: 4 is even but not a multiple of 3.

qa.q: How many divisors does 77 = 7 × 11 have?
Which number shows that 'If n has exactly 4 divisors, then n is a product of two distinct primes' is false?
qa.e: 27 = 3³ has divisors 1, 3, 9, 27: four, but it is not pq.

qa.q: A number has exactly 3 divisors. What must it be?
qa.e: Only p² has the divisors 1, p, p².

qa.q: Why does a perfect square have an odd number of factors?
qa.a: Its square root is a factor that pairs with itself
qa.e: All other factors pair as d and n/d; √n is the unpaired one.

qa.q: 'If corresponding angles are equal, then the lines are parallel.' What is the converse and is it true?
qa.a: If lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal: true
qa.e: Both directions hold for parallel lines and a transversal.

qa.q: Which shape shows that 'If all angles of a quadrilateral are equal, it is a square' is false?
qa.a: A rectangle with sides 4 cm and 7 cm
qa.e: All its angles are 90° but its sides are not all equal.

qa.q: In △ABC with AB = AC, the bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at I and cut AC at E and AB at F. Why is IE = IF?
qa.a: ∠IBC = ∠ICB, so IB = IC; then △IBF ≅ △ICE by ASA
qa.e: Equal base angles have equal halves, so △IBC is isosceles with IB = IC. With the vertically opposite angles at I and the equal half-angles at B and C, ASA gives △IBF ≅ △ICE, so IF = IE.

qa.q: In △ABC with ∠A = 60°, ∠B = 90° and ∠C = 30°, the same lengths IE and IF turn out to be equal. What does this show about the converse 'If IE = IF, then AB = AC'?
qa.a: It is false: here IE = IF but AB ≠ AC
qa.e: AB is opposite the 30° angle and AC is opposite the 90° angle, so AB ≠ AC even though IE = IF. One counterexample is enough to make the converse false.

qa.q: Two unequal sticks are joined at their midpoints at an angle that is not 90°. Their ends form a:
qa.e: Diagonals bisecting each other give a parallelogram; unequal and not perpendicular rules out the others.

qa.q: Two equal sticks are joined at their midpoints. Their ends always form a:
qa.e: Equal diagonals that bisect each other give a rectangle (a square if also perpendicular).

qa.q: Which quadrilateral has equal diagonals but is not a rectangle?
qa.e: Its diagonals are equal but they do not bisect each other.

qa.q: A transversal makes corresponding angles of 72° and 75° with two lines. What can you conclude?
qa.e: If the lines were parallel, corresponding angles would be equal.

qa.q: 'If a = b, then a + 7 = b + 7.' What is its converse, and is it true?
qa.a: If a + 7 = b + 7 then a = b; true
qa.e: Subtracting 7 from both sides gives the converse: cancellation.

qa.q: Which pair shows that 'If x² = y², then x = y' is false?
qa.e: Both squares are 36 but the numbers differ.

qa.q: Is 'If x³ = y³, then x = y' true for real numbers?
qa.e: (−2)³ = −8 and 2³ = 8 differ; cubes keep the sign, so equal cubes force equal numbers.

qa.q: Which statement and converse are BOTH true?
qa.e: Only the cube statement works both ways.

qa.q: Which pair is a counterexample to 'If ab is a perfect square, then a and b are perfect squares'?
qa.e: 3 × 27 = 81 = 9², but neither 3 nor 27 is a perfect square.

qa.q: Why is the product of two perfect squares always a perfect square?
qa.e: Rearranging the factors gives a square of mn.

qa.q: If x² = 49, what are the possible values of x?
qa.e: Both 7² and (−7)² equal 49.

qa.q: Kiran writes: 'a + 3 = b + 3, so a = b.' Which property is he using?
qa.a: Cancellation (the converse of adding the same number)
qa.e: Subtracting 3 from both sides undoes adding 3.

qa.q: Which number is a counterexample to 'If n is divisible by 4 and 6, then n is divisible by 24'?
qa.e: 36 is divisible by 4 and 6 but 36 ÷ 24 = 1.5.

qa.q: Why is 'divisible by 5 and 12 ⇒ divisible by 60' true?
qa.a: 5 and 12 have no common factor, so LCM(5, 12) = 60
qa.e: A number divisible by both is divisible by their LCM, which here is the product.

qa.q: What is LCM(4, 6)?
qa.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12; 12 is also a multiple of 4.

qa.q: Is 4,61,720 divisible by 8?
qa.e: Only the last three digits matter: 720.

qa.q: Why does the last-three-digits test for 8 work?
qa.a: 1000 is divisible by 8, so only the last three digits affect the remainder
qa.e: Any number = 1000 × (something) + last three digits.

qa.q: Which number shows 'divisible by 2 and 4 ⇒ divisible by 8' is false?
qa.e: 20 is divisible by 2 and 4 but not by 8.

qa.q: The four-digit number 47d2 (d is a single digit) is divisible by 3. Which value of d works?
qa.e: Digit sum = 4 + 7 + d + 2 = 13 + d. With d = 2 it is 15, a multiple of 3; with 3, 4 or 6 it is 16, 17 or 19.

qa.q: 'If a number is divisible by 3, then its digit sum is divisible by 3.' Is this converse of the digit-sum test true?
qa.a: Yes, both directions of the test for 3 are true
qa.e: A number and its digit sum leave the same remainder when divided by 3, so both directions hold.

qa.q: What is the smallest n ≥ 1 for which 4n² + 1 is not prime?
For n = 10, what is n² + n + 11?
2¹¹ − 1 = 2047. Which shows it is not prime?
Which value of n is a counterexample to '2ⁿ + 1 is always prime'?
Any common factor of n and n + 3 must divide:
qa.e: If d divides both, it divides (n + 3) − n = 3.

qa.q: Do 21 and 24 have a common factor greater than 1?
qa.a: Yes, 3, because 21 is a multiple of 3

qa.q: n = 20 is not a multiple of 3. What can you say about 20 and 23?
qa.a: They have no common factor except 1
qa.e: The only possible common factor is 3, and 3 does not divide 20.

qa.q: Ravi checks n² + n + 11 for n = 1 to 9 and gets primes every time. What can he conclude?
qa.a: Nothing for all n; checking examples does not prove it, and n = 10 fails
qa.e: Examples can suggest a pattern but cannot prove it.

qa.q: Kabir checks 1 + 3 = 4, 3 + 5 = 8 and 5 + 7 = 12, and says: 'The sum of two odd numbers is always even. Proved!' What is wrong?
qa.a: Examples alone cannot prove a statement for all numbers
qa.e: The statement is true, but checking a few cases is not a proof. A proof must work for every pair of odd numbers, for example using 2m + 1 and 2n + 1.

qa.q: Which expression stands for any odd number, if m is an integer?
qa.e: 2m is always even, so one more than it, 2m + 1, is always odd.

qa.q: The sum of three consecutive integers n, n + 1, n + 2 is 3n + 3. Which number always divides this sum?
qa.e: 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), so the sum is always a multiple of 3. It is not always even: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.

qa.q: What do we call a basic fact that is accepted without proof?
qa.e: Axioms are the starting points of reasoning; theorems are proved from them.

qa.q: (2m + 1)(2n + 1) = 4mn + 2m + 2n + 1. What does this prove about the product of two odd numbers?
qa.e: 4mn + 2m + 2n + 1 = 2(2mn + m + n) + 1, which is one more than an even number, so it is odd.

qa.q: Goldbach's conjecture says every even number greater than 2 is the sum of two primes. What is its status?
qa.a: It has been checked for very many numbers but not yet proved
qa.e: Computers have checked it for enormous numbers, but nobody has found a proof yet, so it is still a conjecture.

qa.q: How many counterexamples are needed to show that a statement about all numbers is false?
qa.e: A claim about ALL cases fails as soon as one case breaks it.

qa.q: In the usual proof that the angles of a triangle add up to 180°, a line is drawn through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. Which fact is used next?
qa.a: Alternate angles made by a transversal with parallel lines are equal
qa.e: The two alternate angles equal two angles of the triangle, and together with the third angle they form a straight angle of 180°.

qa.q: Find the mean of 4, 8, 6, 10 and 7.
qa.e: Sum = 35 and there are 5 values, so the mean is 35 ÷ 5 = 7.

qa.q: Find the median of 3, 9, 1, 7, 6.
qa.e: In order: 1, 3, 6, 7, 9. The middle (3rd) value is 6.

qa.q: Find the median of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.
qa.e: There are 6 values, so the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.

qa.q: Riya scored 72, 85, 90 and 78 in four tests. What must she score in the fifth test to make her mean exactly 80?
qa.e: For a mean of 80 over 5 tests she needs a total of 400. So far she has 325, so she needs 75.

qa.q: What is the mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3, 5?
qa.e: 3 occurs three times, more than any other value.

qa.q: In a class survey, 4 students have 1 pet, 3 have 2 pets and 3 have 3 pets. What is the mean number of pets?
Monthly pocket money of five friends: ₹200, ₹220, ₹250, ₹230 and ₹2000. Which average best shows what is typical?
qa.a: The median, because the mean is pulled up by one very large value
qa.e: The mean is ₹580, which is more than four of the five friends get. The median ₹230 is much more typical.

qa.q: The mean of 10 numbers is 15. Later it is found that 24 was wrongly copied as 42. What is the correct mean?
qa.e: The wrong total is 150. The correct total is 150 − 42 + 24 = 132, so the correct mean is 13.2.

qa.q: A class has 25 boys averaging 62 kg and 15 girls averaging 50 kg. What is the class average weight?
When is the combined average equal to the mean of the two group averages?
qa.a: When the two groups are the same size
qa.e: With equal n, (na + nb)/(2n) = (a + b)/2.

qa.q: Three sections have 20, 30 and 50 students with averages 70, 80 and 60. What is the overall average?
Ravi buys 40 shares at ₹120 and 60 shares at ₹95. What is his average price per share?
A team scores at 7 runs per over for 10 overs and 4 runs per over for the next 40 overs. What is the run rate for the 50 overs?
qa.e: Runs = 70 + 160 = 230 in 50 overs.

qa.q: February (28 days) had average daily rainfall 3 mm and March (31 days) had 5 mm. How should the average daily rainfall for both months be found?
qa.e: Weight each month's average by its number of days.

qa.q: The mean of 20 numbers is 15. A 21st number, 36, is added. What is the new mean?
qa.e: New total = 300 + 36 = 336, divided by 21.

qa.q: The combined average of groups with averages 40 and 70 is 60. Which group is larger?
qa.e: 60 is closer to 70, so that group has more weight.

qa.q: A 5 L bucket of water has 0.4 L of dye. What is the concentration of dye?
4 L of 15% juice is mixed with 1 L of 40% juice. What is the strength of the mixture?
qa.e: Juice = 0.6 + 0.4 = 1 L in 5 L.

qa.q: 2 L of 30% acid is mixed with 6 L of 10% acid. The result is closer to:
qa.a: 10%, because there is more of the 10% solution
qa.e: Result = (0.6 + 0.6)/8 = 15%, which is closer to 10%.

qa.q: What is the strength of the mixture in the previous question?
How much water must be added to 8 L of 25% syrup to make it 20%?
qa.e: Sugar = 2 L. 2 ÷ (8 + x) = 0.2 gives 8 + x = 10.

qa.q: Ananya has 3 L of 40% orange concentrate. She adds water to make a 15% drink. What is the final volume?
A mixture has 30 L of milk and 10 L of water. What percentage is milk?
Equal volumes of 12% and 18% solutions are mixed. What is the strength?
qa.e: With equal volumes, the result is the simple average.

qa.q: 15 g of 20-karat gold is melted with 5 g of 24-karat gold. What is the purity of the alloy, in karats?
In the varna system, how many varna is pure gold?
qa.e: Pure gold is 16 varna in old Indian texts (and 24 karat today).

qa.q: 8 g of 12-varna gold and 8 g of 14-varna gold are melted together. What is the varna of the result?
qa.e: Equal weights, so the simple mean of 12 and 14.

qa.q: A pit is 10 m long. The first 4 m are 3 m deep and the remaining 6 m are 2 m deep. What is its mean depth?
If the pit in the previous question is 2 m wide everywhere, what is its volume?
qa.e: Volume = mean depth × area = 2.4 × 10 × 2.

qa.q: Can you get a 30% salt solution by mixing 10% and 25% solutions?
qa.a: No, the result must lie between 10% and 25%
qa.e: A mixture's strength is a weighted average, so it cannot exceed the stronger solution.

qa.q: Riya wants to turn 5 L of 20% juice into 25% juice by adding water. Solving 1 ÷ (5 + x) = 0.25 gives x = −1. What does this mean?
qa.a: It is impossible by adding water; you would have to remove water
qa.e: A negative amount of water cannot be added.

qa.q: Who among these described rules for mixing gold of different purities?
qa.e: Sridharacharya’s Patiganita (about 750 CE) includes problems on melting together gold of different varnas.

qa.q: Marks 60, 75, 90 are weighted 1 : 1 : 2. What is the weighted average?
A project is graded on idea (weight 2), work (weight 5) and presentation (weight 3). Kabir scores 8, 6 and 9. What is his weighted score?
Riya gets 36/50 in Maths and 18/20 in a quiz. What are these as percentages?
Using those percentages with weights 3 : 1, what is Riya's overall percentage?
A product has ratings: 5★ by 12 people, 4★ by 6, 3★ by 2. What is the average rating?
Why should marks out of different maximums be converted to percentages before weighting?
qa.a: So that each mark is on the same scale
qa.e: 36/50 and 18/20 cannot be compared or combined until they are on a common scale.

qa.q: A school weights homework 20%, tests 30% and the exam 50%. Meena gets 90, 70 and 60. What is her final score?
A restaurant has 40 ratings of 5★ and 10 ratings of 1★. What is the average?
Scores 60 and 100 have weights 3 and 1. What is the weighted mean?
The weights in the previous question are changed to 6 and 2. What is the weighted mean now?
qa.e: Doubling all weights changes nothing: (360 + 200)/8 = 70.

qa.q: Scores 60 and 100 with weights 3 and 1. If 100 is added to both weights (103 and 101), the weighted mean will be:
qa.a: very close to 80, the simple mean
qa.e: Weights 103 and 101 are nearly equal, so the result ≈ (60 + 100)/2. (It is about 79.8.)

qa.q: A shopkeeper buys pens for ₹800 and sells them at 15% profit, and notebooks for ₹1200 sold at 5% profit. What is his overall profit %?
qa.e: Profit = 120 + 60 = 180 on a cost of 2000.

qa.q: Item A costs ₹300 with 20% profit; item B costs ₹700 with 10% profit. Overall profit %?
Why is overall profit % not the simple average of the rates?
qa.a: Items with larger cost carry more weight
qa.e: The total profit depends on how much was spent on each item.

qa.q: Weights 2 : 5 : 3 are scaled to 20 : 50 : 30. The weighted average:
qa.e: Multiplying every weight by 10 cancels out in Σwx ÷ Σw.

qa.q: If every weight is the same, the weighted average equals:
qa.e: Equal weights treat every value alike.

qa.q: Why do the bars of a histogram touch each other?
qa.a: Because the classes are continuous with no gaps between them
qa.e: In a histogram each class ends exactly where the next one begins, so the bars sit side by side.

qa.q: In a frequency polygon, each frequency is plotted against which value of its class?
qa.e: The points of a frequency polygon are at the class marks, the middle of each class.

qa.q: Tickets sold at a school fair: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 15, Thu 40, Fri 30. What is the difference between the highest and lowest day's sales?
qa.e: Highest is Thursday (40) and lowest is Wednesday (15): 40 − 15 = 25.

qa.q: Monthly rainfall in a town: June 120 mm, July 300 mm, August 240 mm, September 150 mm. In which month was the rainfall exactly twice that of June?
qa.e: Twice June's rainfall is 2 × 120 = 240 mm, which is August.

qa.q: Which graph is best for showing how the temperature changed hour by hour on a day?
qa.e: A line graph joins readings taken over time, making rises and falls easy to see.

qa.q: A bar graph compares two shops' sales of 92 and 96 sweets, but its vertical axis starts at 90. Why does it look misleading?
qa.a: The axis does not start at 0, so a small difference looks very large
qa.e: Starting at 90, the bars look like 2 and 6 units tall, so one seems three times the other, though 96 is barely more than 92.

qa.q: In a histogram, class 0–10 has frequency 5 and class 10–30 has frequency 20. Taking width 10 as standard, what should the adjusted height of the 10–30 bar be?
qa.e: The class 10–30 is twice the standard width, so its height is halved: 20 × 10 ÷ 20 = 10.

qa.q: A bar graph shows Riya sold 45 laddoos and Meena sold 62 laddoos at the Diwali stall. How many more did Meena sell?
qa.e: Difference = 62 − 45 = 17 laddoos.

qa.q: Which chart best shows the total number of medals each state won and how many were gold, silver and bronze?
qa.e: The full bar gives the total and the segments give each medal type.

qa.q: Which chart is best for comparing, month by month, the rainfall in Chennai and Mumbai?
qa.e: Bars for the two cities stand side by side in each month.

qa.q: In a 100% stacked bar, what does the full height of every bar represent?
qa.e: Each bar is scaled to its own total, so all reach 100%.

qa.q: A stacked bar for a school has segments: walk 120, bus 200, cycle 80. What is the total?
In that school, what percentage come by bus?
In a 100% stacked chart, Village A's segment for 'farmers' is 70% and Village B's is 40%. What can you say?
qa.a: A larger share of A's workers are farmers
qa.e: 100% bars show shares, not actual numbers.

qa.q: A clustered chart shows a shop's sales of tea and coffee each day. On Monday the bars are 40 and 25. How many more cups of tea were sold?
Class 8: 20 like cricket, 10 football. Class 9: 15 cricket, 15 football. In a 100% stacked chart, what is cricket's share in Class 8?
qa.e: 20 out of 30.

qa.q: In a 100% stacked bar, 'vegetarian' is 60% for Hostel A (total 50) and 60% for Hostel B (total 300). How many vegetarians in Hostel B?
Which statement can be concluded from a 100% stacked chart alone?
qa.a: The share of each part in each bar
qa.e: A 100% chart shows only percentages of each bar's own total.

qa.q: A stacked chart shows Shop X: tea 30, coffee 20; Shop Y: tea 45, coffee 30. In a 100% chart, how do the two bars compare?
qa.a: They look the same: 60% tea and 40% coffee in both

qa.q: A survey shows 72 out of 120 students like maths. What percentage is this?
25% of a family's monthly spending of ₹36,000 is on food. How much is that?
Why can't you get the actual numbers back from a 100% stacked chart?
qa.a: The totals of the bars are not shown
qa.e: Part = % × total, and the total is unknown.

qa.q: In a stacked chart, Team A's runs are 120 (fours) + 80 (others) and Team B's are 90 + 110. Which is a valid conclusion?
qa.a: A scored more runs in fours than B
qa.e: The chart shows A's fours = 120 and B's = 90; it says nothing about sixes, skill or the future.

qa.q: If 30% of the students is 54, how many students are there in all?
Arjun sleeps 9 hours a day. What percentage of the day is this?
A smart watch says 30% of last night's 8 hours was deep sleep. How long was that?
A chart of 2000 objects orbiting the Earth shows: satellites 45%, rocket parts 15%, debris 40%. How many pieces of debris?
In a series, a team took 30 wickets: fast bowlers 18, spinners 12. What share went to spinners?
A pie chart has a slice of 72°. What share of the whole is this?
Why is a set of 100% stacked bars often better than several pie charts?
qa.a: Lengths in bars side by side are easier to compare than angles in separate pies
qa.e: Our eyes compare aligned lengths better than angles.

qa.q: The Sharma family spends ₹12,000 on food out of ₹40,000 in March. What share should the food segment of March's 100% bar show?
In April the family spends ₹13,500 on food out of ₹45,000. Compared to March (30%), the food share is:
qa.e: 13500 ÷ 45000 = 0.3, so the share is unchanged though the amount grew.

qa.q: A chart of threatened animal species in a region shows mammals 120, birds 180, reptiles 60 and amphibians 40. What share of the species are birds?
What is the range of the data 12, 7, 19, 3, 15?
qa.e: Range = highest − lowest = 19 − 3 = 16.

qa.q: What is the class mark of the class 20–30?
qa.e: Class mark = (20 + 30) ÷ 2 = 25, the middle of the class.

qa.q: What is the width of the class 45–60?
qa.e: Class width = upper limit − lower limit = 60 − 45 = 15.

qa.q: Test scores of 10 students: 6, 8, 9, 5, 8, 10, 7, 8, 9, 4. How many students scored 8 or more?
qa.e: The scores 8 or more are 8, 9, 8, 10, 8 and 9: six students.

qa.q: Classes are 0–10, 10–20, 20–30. In which class is a value of exactly 10 counted?
qa.e: In these classes the lower limit is included and the upper limit is not, so 10 goes into 10–20.

qa.q: Harpreet asks her classmates about their favourite festival and records the answers. What kind of data is this?
qa.e: She collected the data herself, first-hand, so it is primary data.

qa.q: A frequency table for the number of siblings shows frequencies 5, 8, 12, 7 and 3. How many students were surveyed?
qa.e: The total number of students is the sum of the frequencies: 5 + 8 + 12 + 7 + 3 = 35.

qa.q: Kabir groups heights that are at least 140 cm and less than 170 cm into classes of width 5 cm (140–145, 145–150, ...). How many classes does he need?
qa.e: The heights cover 170 − 140 = 30 cm, and 30 ÷ 5 = 6 classes: 140–145 up to 165–170.

qa.q: Why is column addition faster than counting dots for big numbers?
qa.a: Its steps depend on the number of digits, not the size of the number
qa.e: A 6-digit sum takes about 6 column steps, while counting would take hundreds of thousands of counts.
Units 12 (carry 1), tens 6 + 7 + 1 = 14 (carry 1), hundreds 8 + 5 + 1 = 14 (carry 1), thousands 5 + 2 + 1 = 8.

qa.q: In 468 + 375, what is written in the tens place of the answer?
qa.e: Units: 8 + 5 = 13, carry 1. Tens: 6 + 7 + 1 = 14, write 4.

qa.q: When adding by columns, which column do you start with?
qa.e: Carries move leftwards, so you must start from the right.

qa.q: What does 'carrying 1' into the tens column really mean?
qa.e: Place value: ten units equal one ten.

qa.q: About how many basic steps would counting on from 3,000 by ones take to add 3,000 + 2,000?
qa.e: You would count 2,000 more ones; column addition needs only 4 column steps.

qa.q: What is the final carry written when adding 875 + 649?
qa.e: 5 + 9 = 14 (carry 1); 7 + 4 + 1 = 12 (carry 1); 8 + 6 + 1 = 15 (write 5, carry 1). The sum is 1524.

qa.q: Riya adds 4999 + 2 by columns. How many carries does she make?
Which is the best description of an algorithm?
qa.a: A finite list of clear steps that solves a problem
qa.e: An algorithm must be step-by-step, precise and finite.

qa.q: Which instruction would be a poor step in an algorithm?
qa.e: 'A little' and 'maybe' are vague; two people could follow this step differently.

qa.q: Start with 5. Repeat 3 times: double the number and then add 1. What is the result?
In an algorithm for making chai, what are the inputs?
qa.a: Water, tea leaves, milk and sugar
qa.e: Inputs are what the algorithm starts with. The cup of chai is the output.

qa.q: Use the rule: if even, halve it; if odd, multiply by 3 and add 1; stop at 1. Starting from 12, how many steps until you reach 1?
Why must an algorithm have a finite number of steps?
qa.a: So that it eventually stops and gives an answer
qa.e: A procedure that never stops can never give an output.

qa.q: Algorithm A: add 3, then multiply by 2. Algorithm B: multiply by 2, then add 3. Both start with 5. What is A's result minus B's result?
qa.e: A gives (5 + 3) × 2 = 16. B gives 5 × 2 + 3 = 13. 16 − 13 = 3, so order matters.

qa.q: To find the largest number in a list, keep a 'biggest so far' and replace it only when a number is BIGGER. For the list 7, 3, 12, 9, 12, 5, how many times is 'biggest so far' replaced after starting with 7?
qa.e: Only the first 12 is bigger than 7. The second 12 is equal, not bigger, so no change.

qa.q: What is the largest possible carry when adding two numbers by columns?
qa.e: The biggest column total is 9 + 9 + 1 (carry) = 19.

qa.q: What is the largest possible column total when adding two numbers (including the carry)?
Adding three numbers, what is the largest possible carry from the units column?

qa.e: Treat 596 as 0596: units 13 (carry 1), tens 2 + 9 + 1 = 12 (carry 1), hundreds 0 + 5 + 1 = 6, thousands 8.

qa.q: Joseph writes 523 + 41 as 523 + 410. What mistake did he make?
qa.a: He lined up from the left; 41 should be 041
qa.e: Units must line up with units: 41 = 041.

qa.q: Kavya buys a pen for ₹45.50 and a notebook for ₹62.75. What is the total?
Use Euclid's algorithm to find HCF(48, 18).
Find HCF(91, 65) using Euclid's algorithm.
To check whether 97 is prime, what is the largest prime you need to try dividing by?
qa.e: √97 is a little less than 10, so you only need to try 2, 3, 5 and 7. None divides 97, so 97 is prime.

qa.q: Riya thinks of a number from 1 to 100. Arjun always guesses the middle of the remaining range and is told 'higher' or 'lower'. What is the most guesses he will ever need?
qa.e: After each wrong guess at most half of the numbers are left: 100 → 50 → 25 → 12 → 6 → 3 → 1. After 6 guesses only one number can remain, so the 7th guess is sure to be right (2⁷ = 128 ≥ 100).

qa.q: HCF(12, 18) = 6. What is LCM(12, 18)?
After using the Sieve of Eratosthenes on the numbers 1 to 100, how many primes are left?
qa.e: Crossing out 1 and the multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7 (but not those primes themselves) leaves exactly 25 primes up to 100.

qa.q: Use repeated subtraction (the older form of Euclid's method) for HCF(35, 14): keep subtracting the smaller from the larger. What is the HCF?
qa.e: (35, 14) → (21, 14) → (7, 14) → (7, 7). When the two numbers are equal, that number, 7, is the HCF.

qa.q: Write 157 = 12 × q + r with 0 ≤ r < 12. What is r?
qa.e: 12 × 13 = 156, so 157 = 12 × 13 + 1. The remainder is 1.

qa.q: In a flowchart, what does a diamond-shaped box show?
qa.e: A diamond holds a question, and the flow splits into 'yes' and 'no' paths.

qa.q: A total starts at 10. A loop runs 5 times, and each time it adds 4 to the total. What is the final total?
qa.e: 5 additions of 4 add 20, so the total becomes 10 + 20 = 30.

qa.q: Set x = 2. While x is less than 100, replace x by x × x. What is the output?
qa.e: 2 → 4 → 16 → 256. 16 is still less than 100, so the loop runs once more, giving 256.

qa.q: Which algorithm finds 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 1000 in the fewest steps?
qa.e: The formula needs just a multiplication and a division: 1000 × 1001 ÷ 2 = 500500, instead of 999 additions.

qa.q: An algorithm says: 'If marks are 33 or more, print Pass; else print Fail.' Meena scores exactly 33. What is printed?
qa.e: 33 or more includes 33 itself, so the condition is true and Pass is printed.

qa.q: Harpreet's algorithm for the average of three numbers says: 'Add them, then divide by 2.' What is the correct average of 6, 9 and 12?
qa.e: The bug is dividing by 2. The correct average is (6 + 9 + 12) ÷ 3 = 27 ÷ 3 = 9.

qa.q: What is it called when you break a big problem, like planning a school trip, into smaller tasks?
qa.e: Decomposition means splitting a problem into parts: booking a bus, collecting money, planning food, and so on.

qa.q: For each of 4 rows, Kabir's algorithm says 'place 6 diyas'. How many times is a diya placed in total?
qa.e: The inner step runs 6 times for each of the 4 rows: 4 × 6 = 24.

qa.q: In the simple divisors(n) algorithm, which numbers j are tested?
qa.e: It checks each j in turn and keeps those that divide n.

qa.q: How many numbers does the simple algorithm test for n = 120?
Using the pair idea, up to what value of j must you check for n = 120?
Why can we stop checking at √n?
qa.a: Divisors pair up as j and n/j, and one of each pair is at most √n
qa.e: If j > √n divides n, then n/j < √n was already found.

qa.q: How many divisors does 100 have?
The simple algorithm takes 1 second for n = 1,000,000. Roughly how long for n = 10,000,000?
qa.e: The work grows in proportion to n.

qa.q: Which list shows all divisors of 28?
For n = 49, the pair method checks j = 1 to 7. Which divisor appears without a partner?
qa.e: 7 × 7 = 49, so 7 pairs with itself.

qa.q: The common divisors of 20 and 30 in sorted order are 1, 2, 5, 10. What is the gcd?
qa.e: The gcd is the last (largest) common divisor.

qa.q: Which list is the common divisors of 16 and 24?
What is gcd(45, 60) by listing divisors?
qa.e: Common divisors: 1, 3, 5, 15.

qa.q: In a sorted list of common divisors, why is the gcd the last element?
qa.a: The list goes from smallest to largest
qa.e: Sorted increasing, the largest is at the end.

qa.q: What is a list in an algorithm?
qa.a: A data structure that stores values in order
qa.e: Lists hold many values like divisors, one after another.

qa.q: Why does the algorithm name results like Dm, Dn and C?
qa.a: So later steps can refer to them clearly
qa.e: Naming intermediate values makes each step precise.

qa.q: How many common divisors do 12 and 18 have?
Two ropes of 28 m and 42 m are cut into pieces of equal length, as long as possible, with nothing left over. How long is each piece?
Using multiples of the larger number, what is LCM(15, 20)?
qa.e: 20, 40, 60; 60 is the first divisible by 15.

qa.q: How many multiples of 9 must you list to find LCM(6, 9)?
qa.e: 9 (not divisible by 6), 18 (divisible by 6). So 2.

qa.q: A = 3, 6, 9, 12 and B = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Which elements of A are not in B?
qa.e: 6 and 12 appear in both; 3 and 9 do not.

qa.q: Why is walking down two sorted lists together efficient?
qa.a: Each element is looked at about once
qa.e: Pointers only move forward, so the work is about the total length of the lists.

qa.q: While walking the lists, the A item is 8 and the B item is 10. What should you do?
qa.a: Record 8 as missing from B and move A's pointer
qa.e: Since B is sorted and already past 8, 8 cannot be in B.

qa.q: Diyas in two rows flash every 4 seconds and every 6 seconds. After how many seconds do they flash together again?
Which is the first multiple of 14 that is divisible by 21?
For LCM by multiples, why list multiples of the larger number?
qa.a: You reach the LCM in fewer steps
qa.e: Bigger jumps reach the common multiple sooner.

qa.q: In the count-up improvement, what is stored instead of full lists?
qa.a: Only the most recent common divisor found
qa.e: Each time a j divides both, it replaces the stored value.

qa.q: When counting down from min(m, n), when can you stop?
qa.a: At the first j that divides both m and n
qa.e: The first common divisor met while counting down is the greatest.

qa.q: Counting down for gcd(45, 75), which j do you reach first that divides both?
qa.e: Start at 45: 75 ÷ 45 is not exact; ... 15 divides both.

qa.q: How many checks does counting down need for gcd(40, 60)?
qa.e: Start at 40 and go down to 20: 40, 39, ..., 20 is 21 numbers.

qa.q: Why is it enough to check j only up to min(m, n)?
qa.a: A common divisor must divide the smaller number, so it cannot exceed it
qa.e: Any divisor of n is at most n.

qa.q: Counting up for gcd(m, n) where m and n are 9-digit numbers could need about how many checks?
qa.e: min(m, n) can be around 10⁸ or more, so that many checks.

qa.q: Which statement about efficiency is correct?
qa.a: Methods whose work grows with the number of digits are much faster for big numbers
qa.e: Digits grow slowly: a 12-digit number has only 12 digits but is about a trillion.

qa.q: A friend improves an algorithm and it runs faster but sometimes gives a wrong gcd. What is the problem?
qa.a: The refinement was not proved correct
qa.e: Correctness must be justified for every change.

qa.q: Using subtraction, gcd(28, 12) becomes gcd(16, 12), then gcd(4, 12). What comes next?
qa.a: Swap to gcd(12, 4), then gcd(8, 4), gcd(4, 4), gcd(0, 4) = 4
qa.e: Keep subtracting the smaller from the larger (swapping as needed) until one number is 0.

qa.q: What is gcd(m, 0)?
qa.e: Every number divides 0, so the greatest common divisor of m and 0 is m.

qa.q: About how many subtractions does gcd(1000, 3) need by the subtraction method?
qa.e: Subtracting 3 from 1000 repeatedly takes 333 steps before the numbers swap.

qa.q: What is 145 mod 12?
Using gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m mod n), find gcd(156, 66).
How many division steps are needed for gcd(1000, 3)?
Why does d divide m mod n if d divides both m and n?
qa.a: m mod n = m − qn, and d divides both m and qn
qa.e: A number dividing two numbers divides their difference.

qa.q: Why is the division method fast even for huge numbers?
qa.a: Its number of steps grows with the number of digits, not the size
qa.e: Remainders shrink quickly, so few steps are needed.

qa.q: The word 'algorithm' comes from the name of:
qa.e: His name in Latin, Algoritmi, became 'algorithm'.

qa.q: Al-Khwarizmi's famous book explained:
qa.a: the Indian decimal numerals and how to calculate with them
qa.e: It spread Indian place-value numerals to the Arab world and later to Europe.

qa.q: By the definition 'exactly two divisors', why is 1 not prime?
qa.e: divisors(1) = 1: a list of length 1.

qa.q: prime(n) reports TRUE when divisors(n) has how many elements?
qa.e: Exactly two divisors: 1 and n.

qa.q: divisors(57) = 1, 3, 19, 57. What does prime(57) report?
qa.e: Four divisors, not two.

qa.q: What are the prime divisors of 90?
qa.e: divisors(90) include 9, 15 etc., but only 2, 3, 5 are prime.

qa.q: How many prime divisors does 210 have?
Which number has exactly 2 divisors?
What is the prime factorisation of 168?
In the algorithm for 360, how many times does 2 divide before moving to 3?
Which list of (prime, power) pairs describes 600?
Using factorisations, what is gcd(2⁴ × 3² × 5, 2² × 3³ × 7)?
qa.e: Common primes: 2 (smaller power 2) and 3 (smaller power 2): 4 × 9.
Common primes 2 and 3 with powers 1 and 1.

qa.q: If two numbers share no prime factor, their gcd is:
qa.e: No common primes means the only common divisor is 1.

qa.q: Why does the factorisation algorithm move to the next prime only when the current one no longer divides?
qa.a: To capture the full power of each prime
qa.e: Dividing repeatedly counts how many times each prime appears.

qa.q: Which number has factorisation pairs (2, 1), (3, 1), (11, 1)?
What does a tiling of the plane require?
qa.a: Copies of shapes that cover it with no gaps and no overlaps
qa.e: Gaps or overlaps are not allowed in a tiling.

qa.q: Which shape can always tile the plane?
qa.e: Translating a parallelogram along its two side directions fills the plane.

qa.q: In quadrilateral WXYZ, which segment is a diagonal?
qa.e: A diagonal joins opposite (non-adjacent) vertices.

qa.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, which side is opposite to BC?
qa.e: BC and DA share no vertex.

qa.q: Which name describes the same quadrilateral as ABCD?
qa.e: DCBA goes round the same vertices in reverse order.

qa.q: Why do we need 'no three of the four points on a line' in the definition?
qa.a: Otherwise two sides would lie along one line and it would collapse into a triangle
qa.e: Three collinear points would make a straight angle, not a true corner.

qa.q: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
qa.e: AC and BD.

qa.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, which pair are adjacent angles?
qa.e: A and B are joined by side AB.

qa.q: A quadrilateral has angles 85°, 95°, 70° and 110°. Is it convex?
qa.a: Yes, all angles are less than 180°
qa.e: Every angle is below 180°.

qa.q: Three angles of a non-convex quadrilateral are 25°, 35° and 20°. What is the reflex angle?
In a non-convex quadrilateral, how many interior angles can be reflex?
qa.e: The four angles add to 360°, so two reflex angles (each > 180°) are impossible.

qa.q: Where do the diagonals of a convex quadrilateral meet?
qa.e: In a convex quadrilateral the diagonals cross inside.

qa.q: Which figure is self-intersecting?
qa.a: A bow-tie whose two sides cross
qa.e: Two of its sides cross each other at a point that is not a vertex.

qa.q: A 4-gon whose four vertices are not all in one plane is called:
qa.e: Its vertices do not lie on one flat surface.

qa.q: In an arrowhead ABCD with the dent at C, what kind of angle is the interior angle at C?
qa.e: At the dent the inside angle is more than 180°.

qa.q: Which statement fits a Venn diagram of 4-gons?
qa.a: Convex quadrilaterals are a subset of all quadrilaterals, which are a subset of 4-gons
qa.e: 4-gons include quadrilaterals (simple, planar) and other types like bow-ties and non-planar figures.

qa.q: In a four-bar linkage, what stays fixed as it moves?
qa.a: The lengths of the four bars
qa.e: The joints turn, so angles and diagonals change but bar lengths do not.

qa.q: A rhombus-shaped linkage of 4 equal bars is pushed. Which shape can it NOT become?
qa.a: A rectangle that is not a square
qa.e: All sides stay equal, so it is always a rhombus (a square at one moment), never a non-square rectangle.

qa.q: What does a pantograph do?
qa.a: Copies a drawing at a larger or smaller size
qa.e: Its parallelogram linkage keeps the copy similar to the original.

qa.q: Four points have no three in a line. How many different 4-gons can be formed using all four as vertices?
qa.e: The orders ABCD, ABDC and ACBD give the only distinct figures.

qa.q: Four points form a convex shape. How many of the 4-gons are self-intersecting?
qa.e: Only one ordering goes round the outside; the other two make bow-ties.

qa.q: Point D is inside triangle ABC. How many non-convex quadrilaterals can be formed with A, B, C, D as vertices?
qa.e: Each choice of where to insert D between two of A, B, C gives an arrowhead.

qa.q: Two forces act on a box along two sides of a parallelogram. By the parallelogram rule, the combined force is shown by:
qa.a: the diagonal from the common corner
qa.e: The resultant is the diagonal of the parallelogram formed by the two forces.

qa.q: Which mechanism helped steam engines move a piston rod in a nearly straight line?
qa.e: James Watt designed a linkage using a parallelogram for this.

qa.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
qa.e: The angles add up to 360°, so the fourth angle is 360° − (80° + 95° + 110°) = 360° − 285° = 75°.

qa.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
qa.e: There are 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 parts, so one part is 36°. The largest angle is 4 × 36° = 144°.

qa.q: Which statement is always true?
qa.e: A square has four equal sides, so it is a special rhombus. The others are true only sometimes.

qa.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it?
qa.e: A quadrilateral with only one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium. Parallelograms and rhombuses have two pairs.

qa.q: Which quadrilateral has two pairs of equal adjacent sides and diagonals that cross at right angles, but need not have parallel sides?
qa.e: That is a kite, like the ones flown on Makar Sankranti.

qa.q: A rhombus has equal diagonals. What special quadrilateral is it?
qa.e: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle. A rhombus that is also a rectangle is a square.

qa.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of a convex quadrilateral, taking one at each vertex?
qa.e: Walking once round any convex polygon you turn through one full turn, 360°.

qa.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x + 10°, x + 20° and x + 30°. What is the largest angle?
qa.e: 4x + 60° = 360°, so x = 75°. The largest angle is x + 30° = 105°.

qa.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
qa.e: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: 180° − 70° = 110°.

qa.q: In parallelogram ABCD the diagonals meet at O, and AC = 16 cm. What is AO?
qa.e: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AO = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.

qa.q: A parallelogram has sides 9 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
qa.e: Opposite sides are equal, so the perimeter is 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 cm.

qa.q: Two opposite angles of a parallelogram are (3x − 10)° and (2x + 20)°. What is the size of each of these angles?
qa.e: Opposite angles are equal: 3x − 10 = 2x + 20, so x = 30. Each angle is 3 × 30 − 10 = 80°.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT always true for a parallelogram?
qa.e: Equal diagonals happen only when the parallelogram is a rectangle (or square).

qa.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm. What is the length of each side?
qa.e: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right triangles with legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Side = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm.

qa.q: Which condition guarantees that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?
qa.a: One pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel
qa.e: If one pair of opposite sides is equal AND parallel, the quadrilateral must be a parallelogram. Just equal is not enough: an isosceles trapezium has one pair of equal opposite sides.

qa.q: Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller angle?
qa.e: Adjacent angles add to 180°. 180° ÷ 5 = 36°, so the angles are 72° and 108°.

qa.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = CD = 7 cm and BC = DA = 4 cm. What must ABCD be?
qa.e: Both pairs of opposite sides are equal.

qa.q: Which congruence rule proves that equal opposite sides make a parallelogram?
qa.e: The diagonal splits it into triangles with three equal sides.

qa.q: What does CPCT stand for?
qa.e: Once triangles are congruent, their matching parts are equal.

qa.q: The diagonals of quadrilateral KLMN meet at O. KO = 6, OM = 6, LO = 4, ON = 9. Is KLMN a parallelogram?
qa.a: No, O is not the midpoint of LN
qa.e: Both diagonals must be bisected.

qa.q: In the proof that bisecting diagonals give a parallelogram, which angles are used as equal in △AOB and △COD?
qa.a: The vertically opposite angles at O
qa.e: ∠AOB = ∠COD as vertically opposite angles, giving SAS.

qa.q: AB ∥ DC and AB = DC = 9 cm in quadrilateral ABCD. What is ABCD?
qa.e: One pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is enough.

qa.q: Which single fact is NOT enough to prove a parallelogram?
qa.a: One pair of opposite sides parallel
qa.e: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides but is not a parallelogram.

qa.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, PQ = 3x − 1 and SR = x + 7, and PQ ∥ SR. For what x is PQRS a parallelogram?
qa.e: Equal and parallel: 3x − 1 = x + 7 gives x = 4.

qa.q: A parallelogram has equal diagonals. What special parallelogram is it?
qa.e: Equal diagonals force all angles to be 90°.

qa.q: A parallelogram's diagonals cross at 90°. What is it?
qa.e: Perpendicular diagonals in a parallelogram make all sides equal.

qa.q: A quadrilateral (not known to be a parallelogram) has perpendicular diagonals. Which can it be without being a rhombus?
qa.e: Kites have perpendicular diagonals but unequal adjacent pairs.

qa.q: In parallelogram PQRS, diagonal PR bisects ∠P. What can you conclude?
qa.e: ∠QPR = ∠RPS = ∠QRP (alternate angles), so △PQR is isosceles with PQ = QR.

qa.q: The angle bisectors of a parallelogram enclose which shape?
qa.e: Each meeting angle is 90°, since half of 180° is 90°.

qa.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 64°. The bisectors of ∠A and ∠D meet at Q. What is ∠AQD?
A parallelogram has diagonals of 10 cm each that cross at right angles. What is it?
qa.e: Equal and perpendicular diagonals in a parallelogram make a square.

qa.q: A quadrilateral has equal diagonals that do not bisect each other. Which can it be?
qa.e: Rectangles and squares have bisecting diagonals.

qa.q: In triangle ABC, D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC, and BC = 14 cm. What is DE?
qa.e: By the mid-point theorem, DE = ½ BC = 7 cm.

qa.q: D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC of triangle ABC. If DE = 4.5 cm, what is BC?
qa.e: DE is half of BC, so BC = 2 × 4.5 = 9 cm.

qa.q: A triangle has sides 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of its sides?
qa.e: Each side of the new triangle is half of a side of the old one, so its perimeter is ½ × 30 = 15 cm.

qa.q: D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC in triangle ABC. DE is parallel to which side?
qa.e: The segment joining the mid-points of two sides is parallel to the third side, BC.

qa.q: In triangle ABC, a line through the mid-point of AB is drawn parallel to BC. Where does it meet AC?
qa.e: By the converse of the mid-point theorem, the line bisects AC.

qa.q: Aisha joins the mid-points of the sides of an irregular quadrilateral, in order. What shape does she always get?
qa.e: Each pair of opposite sides of the new shape is parallel to (and half of) the same diagonal, so it is always a parallelogram.

qa.q: The diagonals of a rectangle are 10 cm long. What is the perimeter of the quadrilateral formed by joining the mid-points of its sides?
qa.e: Each side of the new shape is half of a diagonal, so each side is 5 cm. It is a rhombus with perimeter 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

qa.q: A triangle has area 48 cm². What is the area of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of its three sides?
qa.e: Joining the mid-points makes 4 congruent triangles, so the middle one has ¼ of the area: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm².

qa.q: In the proof of the midpoint theorem, DE is extended to F with EF = DE. Which triangles are congruent?
qa.e: AE = EC, DE = EF and vertically opposite angles at E give SAS.

qa.q: Why is DBCF a parallelogram in that proof?
qa.a: CF is equal and parallel to DB
qa.e: From the congruence, CF = AD = DB and CF ∥ AB.

qa.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 9 cm and 17 cm. What is the length of its mid-segment?
A trapezium's mid-segment is 15 cm and one base is 11 cm. What is the other base?
Three parallel lines cut segments of 4 cm and 4 cm on one transversal. On another transversal the first segment is 6 cm. What is the second?
qa.e: Equal intercepts on one transversal mean equal intercepts on every transversal.

qa.q: To divide a 16 cm segment in the ratio 1 : 3, how many equal steps do you mark on the ray?
qa.e: 1 + 3 = 4 equal steps.

qa.q: A 35 cm rod is divided in the ratio 2 : 5. How long is the longer part?
The mid-segment of a trapezium is parallel to:
qa.e: It runs halfway between the two bases and is parallel to both.

qa.q: What does a median of a triangle join?
qa.a: A vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side
qa.e: That is the definition of a median.

qa.q: Median PM of △PQR is 15 cm. How far is the centroid from P?
The centroid G is 4 cm from the midpoint of side BC on median AD. How long is AD?
qa.e: GD is one-third of AD.

qa.q: In what ratio does the centroid divide each median, from the vertex?
qa.e: The vertex-side part is twice the other.

qa.q: A triangular plate has vertices A(0, 0), B(6, 0), C(0, 9). The centroid is the average of the vertices. Where is it?
Why are the medians called concurrent?
qa.a: All three pass through one point
qa.e: Concurrent lines meet at a single point.

qa.q: AD is a median of length 21 cm, and G is the centroid. What is AG − GD?
qa.e: AG = 14, GD = 7, difference 7.

qa.q: To trisect segment AD using a centroid, which construction works?
qa.a: Make AD a median of a triangle; the centroid is one-third of the way from D
qa.e: The centroid divides AD in 2 : 1, giving a trisection point.

qa.q: A kite has perpendicular diagonals. What is its Varignon figure?
qa.e: Varignon sides are parallel to the diagonals, so they meet at right angles.

qa.q: An isosceles trapezium has equal diagonals. What is its Varignon figure?
qa.e: Each Varignon side is half a diagonal, so all four sides are equal.

qa.q: A quadrilateral's diagonals are 9 cm and 13 cm. What is the perimeter of its Varignon parallelogram?
qa.e: Two sides of 4.5 and two of 6.5: total = 9 + 13.

qa.q: A square has diagonals of 8 cm. What is its Varignon figure?
qa.e: Equal, perpendicular diagonals give a square with sides half a diagonal.

qa.q: In tiling with any quadrilateral, each copy is rotated by how much about an edge midpoint?
qa.e: A half-turn about the midpoint swaps the two ends of that edge.

qa.q: Why do four copies of any quadrilateral fit around a point in such a tiling?
qa.a: Its four angles add up to 360°
qa.e: Each of the four different angles appears once at the point, filling 360°.

qa.q: A quadrilateral has area 50 cm². What is the area of its Varignon parallelogram?
qa.e: The Varignon parallelogram has half the area.

qa.q: Which tiling idea uses the Varignon parallelograms of copies?
qa.a: They form a parallelogram grid showing how translated copies fit
qa.e: A parallelogram grid tiles the plane, guiding the placement of the copies.

qa.q: What is each interior angle of a regular pentagon?
qa.e: Sum of angles = 540°; 540 ÷ 5 = 108.

qa.q: Why can't regular pentagons tile the plane?
qa.a: 360° is not a whole-number multiple of 108°
qa.e: Around a point the angles must add up to exactly 360°.

qa.q: Which regular polygon can tile the plane on its own?
What is special about the 'hat' shape found in 2023?
qa.a: It tiles the plane, but only in a pattern that never repeats
qa.e: It is an aperiodic monotile.

qa.q: Can an arrowhead (non-convex) quadrilateral tile the plane?
qa.e: Half-turns about edge midpoints work for any quadrilateral.

qa.q: In a bow-tie 4-gon, the two crossing sides make an angle of 40° inside each of the two triangles of the bow-tie. What is the sum of its four vertex angles?
Joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle with area 36 cm² cuts it into 4 congruent triangles. What is the area of each?
What does 'scissors congruence' mean?
qa.a: Cutting a shape into pieces that can be rearranged into another shape
qa.e: The pieces are rearranged without overlap or gaps.

qa.q: Which ordered pair is a solution of 2x + y = 7?
A pen costs ₹x and a notebook costs ₹y. 2 pens and 3 notebooks cost ₹110. Which equation shows this?
qa.e: Cost of 2 pens = 2x and of 3 notebooks = 3y. Together: 2x + 3y = 110.

qa.q: If (k, 2) is a solution of 3x − 2y = 8, what is k?
qa.e: Substitute x = k, y = 2: 3k − 4 = 8, so 3k = 12 and k = 4.

qa.q: How many solutions does x + y = 10 have?
qa.e: For every value of x there is a matching y = 10 − x, such as (1, 9), (2.5, 7.5), (−3, 13), and so on.

qa.q: Write 4x − 5y + 6 = 0 in the form ax + by + c = 0. What is b?
qa.e: Compare term by term: a = 4, b = −5, c = 6. The sign belongs to the coefficient.

qa.q: For x + 2y = 12, find y when x = 4.
How can y = 3 be written as a linear equation in two variables?
qa.e: The coefficient of x is 0, so x can take any value while y stays 3.

qa.q: A box holds 60 sweets: x laddoos and y pedas. Which equation describes the box?
qa.e: The numbers of laddoos and pedas together make 60.

qa.q: Write 2y = 5 − 3x in the form ax + by + c = 0. What is c?
Write x/3 − y/4 = 2 in standard form with integers. What is b?
qa.e: Multiply by 12: 4x − 3y = 24, so 4x − 3y − 24 = 0.

qa.q: Which equation has exactly the same solutions as 3x − y = 4?
A shop sells chai at ₹15 and samosas at ₹10. Riya buys x chai and y samosas for ₹95. Which equation is correct?
qa.e: Cost of chai 15x plus cost of samosas 10y.

qa.q: Which solution of x + y = 1 lies in Quadrant II?
qa.e: x negative, y positive, and −3 + 4 = 1.

qa.q: Is (−2, −7) a solution of 3x − y = 1?
Why can't we multiply an equation by 0 to get an equivalent one?
qa.a: It becomes 0 = 0, true for every pair
qa.e: Multiplying by 0 destroys the information in the equation.

qa.q: A student models '3 kg of rice and 2 kg of dal cost ₹400' as 3x + 2y = 400 with x = price of dal. What is wrong?
qa.a: x should be the price of rice per kg, since it is multiplied by 3 kg of rice
qa.e: Each coefficient must go with the matching item.

qa.q: What does the graph of x = 4 look like?
qa.e: Every point has x = 4 and any y, so the points form a vertical line crossing the x-axis at (4, 0).

qa.q: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 cut the x-axis?
qa.e: On the x-axis y = 0, so 2x = 12 and x = 6. The point is (6, 0).

qa.q: Where does the line 2x + 3y = 12 cut the y-axis?
qa.e: On the y-axis x = 0, so 3y = 12 and y = 4. The point is (0, 4).

qa.q: Which line passes through the origin?
qa.e: Put x = 0 in y = 5x: y = 0, so (0, 0) is on the line. The others do not contain (0, 0).

qa.q: The point (2, k) lies on the line y = 3x − 1. What is k?
What does the graph of y = −2 look like?
qa.a: A horizontal line 2 units below the x-axis
qa.e: Every point has y = −2, so the line is horizontal and lies 2 units below the x-axis.

qa.q: Where do the lines x = 3 and y = −1 meet?
qa.e: The meeting point must have x = 3 and y = −1, so it is (3, −1).

qa.q: The line x + y = 6 makes a triangle with the two axes. What is the area of this triangle?
qa.e: The line meets the axes at (6, 0) and (0, 6). The triangle has base 6 and height 6, so area = ½ × 6 × 6 = 18.

qa.q: Find the slope of the line through (−3, 1) and (5, 5).
qa.e: Rise 4, run 8.

qa.q: What is the slope of the line through (4, −2) and (4, 7)?
qa.e: Run = 4 − 4 = 0, and we cannot divide by 0. The line is vertical.

qa.q: What is the slope of the line y = 6?
qa.e: It is horizontal: no rise.

qa.q: A ramp must have slope at most 1/12. How long (horizontally) must it be to rise 90 cm?
A ghat road rises 150 m over a horizontal distance of 2 km. What is its slope?
A line has slope 4 and passes through (1, 3). What is y when x = 3?
qa.e: Run 2, rise 8: 3 + 8.

qa.q: A line falls 3 units for every 5 units it goes right. What is its slope?
qa.e: Falling means negative: −3 ÷ 5.

qa.q: Points A(1, 2), B(3, 6), C(6, 12): is the slope AB the same as BC?
qa.a: Yes, both are 2, so A, B, C lie on one line

qa.q: What is the slope of 3x + 4y − 12 = 0?
What is the y-intercept of 3x + 4y − 12 = 0?
Which line is parallel to y = 5x − 2?
qa.e: 10x − 2y = 3 gives y = 5x − 1.5: slope 5.

qa.q: A tank fills at 3 litres per minute starting empty. Which equation gives the litres y after x minutes?
qa.e: Slope 3, intercept 0.

qa.q: Using F = (9/5)C + 32, what is the slope and what does it mean?
qa.e: The slope is the change in F per unit change in C.

qa.q: Write y = (2/3)x − 4 in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integers. Which is correct?
qa.e: Multiply by 3: 3y = 2x − 12, so 2x − 3y − 12 = 0.

qa.q: Lines y = mx + 4 and y = −3x + 1 are parallel. What is m?
qa.e: Parallel lines have equal slopes.

qa.q: A mobile plan charges ₹99 fixed plus ₹10 per GB. In y = mx + d, what are m and d?
qa.e: The rate is the slope and the fixed charge is the intercept.

qa.q: Solve x + y = 12 and x − y = 4.
qa.e: Adding gives 2x = 16, so x = 8; then y = 12 − 8 = 4. Check: 8 − 4 = 4 ✓.

qa.q: 2 pens and 1 notebook cost ₹50. 1 pen and 1 notebook cost ₹35. What is the cost of one pen?
qa.e: Subtract the second bill from the first: the extra pen costs 50 − 35 = ₹15.

qa.q: How many solutions does the pair y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 have?
qa.e: Both lines have slope 2 but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never meet.

qa.q: How many solutions does the pair x + 2y = 4 and 2x + 4y = 8 have?
qa.e: The second equation is just the first multiplied by 2, so both describe the same line. Every point on it is a solution.

qa.q: Solve y = 3x and x + y = 20. What is y?
qa.e: Substitute y = 3x: x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20, x = 5 and y = 15.

qa.q: Kabir is 4 years older than Aisha. The sum of their ages is 30. How old is Aisha?
qa.e: Let Aisha be a and Kabir k: k = a + 4 and a + k = 30. So 2a + 4 = 30, a = 13 and Kabir is 17.

qa.q: On a graph, how do you read off the solution of a pair of linear equations?
qa.a: The point where the two lines meet
qa.e: Only the meeting point lies on both lines, so only it satisfies both equations.

qa.q: At a zoo, adult tickets cost ₹60 and child tickets ₹40. A group buys 10 tickets for ₹480. How many adult tickets did they buy?
qa.e: Let a adults and c children: a + c = 10 and 60a + 40c = 480. Then 60a + 40(10 − a) = 480, so 20a = 80 and a = 4.

qa.q: Two laddoos and one barfi cost ₹50. One laddoo and one barfi cost ₹35. What does one laddoo cost?
qa.e: Taking away the second order from the first leaves one laddoo: 50 − 35.

qa.q: Using that laddoo price, what does one barfi cost?
Solve by comparison: y = 4x − 3 and y = 2x + 5. What is x?
qa.e: 4x − 3 = 2x + 5 gives 2x = 8.

qa.q: For the pair above, what is y?
In the comparison method, what must you do first?
qa.a: Make the same variable the subject of both equations
qa.e: Then the two expressions can be set equal.

qa.q: A puzzle: 🍎 + 🍎 + 🍎 = 30 and 🍎 + 🍌 = 16. What is 🍌?
Solve by comparison: x = 2y + 1 and x = 5y − 8. What is y?
qa.e: 2y + 1 = 5y − 8 gives 9 = 3y.

qa.q: Why should you check your answer in BOTH equations?
qa.a: A solution of the pair must satisfy both
qa.e: A slip in one step may give a pair that fits only one equation.

qa.q: How many solutions does the pair 2x + y = 7 and 4x + 2y = 14 have?
qa.e: All three ratios equal 1/2: the same line.

qa.q: How many solutions does x − 3y = 2 and 2x − 6y = 7 have?
qa.e: 1/2 = −3/−6 = 1/2, but 2/7 ≠ 1/2: parallel lines.

qa.q: How many solutions does 3x + 2y = 8 and x − y = 1 have?
qa.e: 3/1 ≠ 2/(−1), so the lines cross.

qa.q: While solving a pair, Riya ends up with 0 = 0. What does this mean?
qa.a: The equations describe the same line: infinitely many solutions
qa.e: 0 = 0 is always true, so every solution of one is a solution of the other.

qa.q: While solving a pair, Kabir gets 0 = 6. What does this mean?
qa.a: The lines are parallel: no solution
qa.e: A false statement means no pair can satisfy both.

qa.q: For what value of k are kx + 6y = 4 and 2x + 3y = 5 parallel?
Which equation, paired with 2x − 5y = 3, gives coincident lines?
Which equation, paired with x + 4y = 8, gives lines that cross at one point?
qa.e: 1/2 ≠ 4/(−1), so they intersect.

qa.q: The sum of two numbers is 45 and their difference is 13. What is the larger number?
qa.e: x + y = 45, x − y = 13: add to get 2x = 58.

qa.q: Five years ago, Neha was 3 times as old as her brother. Now the sum of their ages is 30. How old is Neha now?
A wallet has ₹10 and ₹50 notes, 16 notes in all, worth ₹400. How many ₹50 notes?
The digits of a two-digit number add to 11. Reversing the digits makes it 45 more. What is the number?
The incomes of A and B are in ratio 5 : 4 and their spending in ratio 7 : 5. Each saves ₹3000. What is A's income?
qa.e: 5k − 7m = 3000 and 4k − 5m = 3000. Subtracting gives k = 2m; so 3m = 3000, m = 1000, k = 2000.

qa.q: 3 chairs and 2 tables cost ₹4300; 2 chairs and 3 tables cost ₹4700. What does one table cost?
qa.e: Add: 5(c + t) = 9000, so c + t = 1800. Subtract: t − c = 400. So t = 1100.

qa.q: A taxi charges a fixed amount plus a rate per km. 10 km costs ₹150 and 15 km costs ₹200. What is the fixed charge?
A fraction x/y: if 2 is added to both parts it becomes 2/3, and if 3 is subtracted from both it becomes 1/2. What is the fraction?
In Mahaviracharya's problem, 9x + 7y = 107 and 7x + 9y = 101. Adding gives 16x + 16y = 208. What is x + y?
Subtracting the equations gives 2x − 2y = 6. With x + y = 13, what is the price of a citron (x)?
qa.e: x − y = 3 and x + y = 13 give 2x = 16.

qa.q: Which ancient text from China solved pairs of equations with a method like elimination?
qa.a: The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art
qa.e: Its 'fangcheng' method combined rows of coefficients.

qa.q: Plan P: ₹200 fixed + ₹2 per unit. Plan Q: ₹50 fixed + ₹5 per unit. At how many units do they cost the same?
For 80 units, which plan (P or Q above) is cheaper?
Two lines drawn on graph paper meet at (4, 3). What should you do next?
qa.e: Graph readings can be slightly off; substituting confirms the answer.

qa.q: Riya walks at 4 km/h starting at 0 km; Arjun cycles at 12 km/h starting 2 hours later from the same place. Using d = 4t and d = 12(t − 2), when does Arjun catch up?
qa.e: 4t = 12t − 24 gives 8t = 24.

qa.q: Two cost lines for plans are parallel. What does this mean?
qa.a: One plan is always cheaper by the same amount
qa.e: Parallel lines never meet, so the gap between costs never changes.

qa.q: Which unit measures volume?
qa.e: Volume counts unit cubes.

qa.q: A stack of 25 identical sheets, each 30 cm × 20 cm and 0.1 cm thick, forms a cuboid. What is its volume?
qa.e: Base area 600 cm² × height 2.5 cm.

qa.q: Cuboids 1 × 2 × 8 and 2 × 2 × 4 have the same volume. Which has the smaller surface area?
Why do cold-region houses tend to be compact rather than long and thin?
qa.a: Less surface area for the same volume means less heat loss
qa.e: Heat escapes through the surface; a compact shape has less of it.

qa.q: The face areas of a cuboid are 24 cm², 32 cm² and 48 cm². What is its volume?
Which surface area is the smallest for a volume of 27 cm³?
qa.e: The cube is the most compact: 6 × 9 = 54. The others are 110 and 78.

qa.q: A rectangular tank has base area 2.5 m² and water 0.8 m deep. What volume of water does it hold?
qa.e: Volume = base area × height.

qa.q: What does surface area measure?
qa.a: The total area of all the outer faces
qa.e: It is the area you would cover if you wrapped the solid.

qa.q: Find the total surface area of a cube of edge 5 cm.
qa.e: A cube has 6 square faces, each 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Total = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

qa.q: Find the total surface area of a cuboid 10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm.
Find the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
Arjun paints the four walls of a room 5 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high at ₹20 per m². What does it cost?
qa.e: Area of four walls = 2(5 + 4) × 3 = 54 m². Cost = 54 × 20 = ₹1080.

qa.q: If the edge of a cube is doubled, what happens to its surface area?
qa.e: Surface area is 6a². With edge 2a it becomes 6(2a)² = 24a², which is 4 times 6a².

qa.q: A road roller is a cylinder of radius 0.7 m and length 2 m. How much ground does it level in 10 full turns? (Use π = 22/7.)
qa.e: In one turn it covers its curved surface: 2 × 22/7 × 0.7 × 2 = 8.8 m². In 10 turns: 88 m².

qa.q: An open box (no lid) measures 10 cm × 8 cm × 5 cm. What is the area of cardboard needed?
qa.e: Four walls: 2(10 + 8) × 5 = 180 cm². Add the base 10 × 8 = 80 cm². Total = 260 cm².

qa.q: Find the total surface area of a closed cylindrical drum of radius 14 cm and height 6 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
How many 2 cm cubes fit in a box 12 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm?
How many matchboxes 5 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm fit in a carton 50 cm × 30 cm × 20 cm (same orientation)?
A 6 × 6 × 6 painted cube is cut into unit cubes. How many have exactly 3 faces painted?
qa.e: Only the 8 corners have 3 painted faces, whatever the size.

qa.q: For the 6 × 6 × 6 cube, how many unit cubes have exactly 2 faces painted?
For the 6 × 6 × 6 cube, how many have exactly 1 face painted?
For the 6 × 6 × 6 cube, how many have no paint?
Which cuboid with whole-number edges has surface area 22 cm²?
A box 9 cm × 9 cm × 9 cm is packed with 2 cm cubes. How many fit?
qa.e: Only 4 fit along each 9 cm edge (4 × 2 = 8 cm): 4 × 4 × 4.

qa.q: Which description fits a right circular cylinder?
qa.a: Two equal circular bases with the axis perpendicular to them
qa.e: That is the definition.

qa.q: A stack of 40 coins, each of radius 1 cm and thickness 0.2 cm, forms a cylinder. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
The radius of a cylinder is tripled and the height is unchanged. Its volume becomes:
qa.e: Volume depends on r²: 3² = 9.

qa.q: Cylinder P has r = 2, h = 9; cylinder Q has r = 3, h = 4. What is the ratio of their volumes P : Q?
The radius of a cylindrical tank is increased by 20%, height unchanged. By what percentage does its volume increase?
The height of a cylinder is halved and its radius doubled. The volume becomes:
Why is V = πr²h for a cylinder?
qa.a: It is a stack of discs of area πr² piled to height h
qa.e: Base area × height, like any prism.

qa.q: A cylindrical glass has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Another has radius 6 cm and height 2.5 cm. Which holds more?
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
Find the volume of a cone with radius 7 cm and height 12 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
Find the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same height. How many cones of water fill the cylinder?
qa.e: The cone's volume is ⅓πr²h, one third of the cylinder's πr²h, so 3 cones fill it.

qa.q: A water tank is a cuboid 2 m long, 1.5 m wide and 1 m deep. How many litres does it hold when full?
qa.e: Volume = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 m³, and 1 m³ = 1000 litres, so the tank holds 3000 litres.

qa.q: Find the volume of a hemispherical bowl of radius 21 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
qa.e: V = (2/3)πr³ = 2/3 × 22/7 × 9261 = 19404 cm³, half of the whole sphere.

qa.q: A metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm. How many small spheres are made?
qa.e: Volume grows with r³. (6 ÷ 2)³ = 3³ = 27, so the big sphere has 27 times the volume of a small one.

qa.q: A cube has total surface area 150 cm². What is its volume?
qa.e: 6a² = 150 gives a² = 25 and a = 5 cm. Volume = 5³ = 125 cm³.

qa.q: A right triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm is rotated about the 4 cm leg. What is the radius of the cone?
qa.e: The leg it spins around is the height; the other leg sweeps out the radius.

qa.q: For the same rotation, what is the slant height?
qa.e: The hypotenuse √(9 + 16) = 5 becomes the slant height.

qa.q: A conical tent has radius 7 m and height 24 m. How much canvas is needed? (π = 22/7)
How much air is inside that tent? (π = 22/7)
A conical paper cup holds 240 ml when full. How much does it hold when filled to half its depth?
qa.e: The water cone has half the radius and half the height: 1/8 of 240.

qa.q: A heap of sand is a cone of radius 3 m and slant height 5 m. What area of tarpaulin covers it? (π = 3.14)
A clown's cap has radius 10 cm and slant height 21 cm. How much paper is needed? (π = 22/7)
Rotating a right triangle about its hypotenuse gives:
qa.a: two cones joined at their bases
qa.e: Each part of the triangle on either side of the altitude sweeps a cone.

qa.q: A cone has radius 7 cm and height 24 cm. What is its slant height?
Find the curved surface area of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
qa.e: Surface area = 4πr² = 4 × 22/7 × 49 = 616 cm².

qa.q: Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
qa.e: TSA = curved part + flat circle = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr² = 3 × 22/7 × 49 = 462 cm².

qa.q: A joker's cap is a cone of radius 7 cm and slant height 12 cm. How much sheet is needed to make it? (Use π = 22/7.)
qa.e: A cap has no base, so we need only the curved surface: πrl = 22/7 × 7 × 12 = 264 cm².

qa.q: A ball has surface area 154 cm². What is its radius? (Use π = 22/7.)
A hemispherical bowl has radius 10.5 cm. What is the area of its inner curved surface? (Use π = 22/7.)
qa.e: Curved surface of a hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 10.5 × 10.5 = 693 cm².

qa.q: Find the total surface area of a solid cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 25 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
What is the volume of a pyramid with base area 48 cm² and height 9 cm?
A square pyramid has base side 10 m and height 12 m. What is its volume?
How many triangular faces does a pentagonal pyramid have?
qa.e: One for each side of the base.

qa.q: A square pyramid has base side 8 cm and slant height 5 cm. What is its total surface area?
Why is a cone like a pyramid?
qa.a: Both have a base and an apex, and V = ⅓ × base area × height for both
qa.e: A cone is a pyramid whose base is a circle.

qa.q: A tent is a square pyramid of base side 4 m and height 3 m. How much air is inside?
A pyramid and a prism have the same base and height. How do their volumes compare?
qa.a: The pyramid has one-third of the prism's volume
qa.e: Pyramid = ⅓ base × height; prism = base × height.

qa.q: What is the apex of a pyramid?
qa.a: The point where the triangular faces meet
qa.e: All side faces meet at the apex.

qa.q: What is the surface area of a sphere of radius 3.5 cm? (π = 22/7)
A sphere of radius 6 cm sits snugly in a cylinder. What is the cylinder's height?
qa.e: The cylinder's height equals the sphere's diameter.

qa.q: For a sphere of radius r, what is the curved surface area of its enclosing cylinder?
qa.e: 2πr × 2r.

qa.q: A sphere has volume 288π cm³. What is the volume of its enclosing cylinder?
qa.e: Sphere = ⅔ cylinder, so cylinder = 288π × 3/2.

qa.q: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm in terms of π.
In the string activity, string covering a whole ball fills how many circles of the ball's radius?
qa.e: Surface area = 4πr² = 4 circles of area πr².

qa.q: What fraction of a cylinder's volume does a sphere fill if it just fits inside?
A laddoo has diameter 4 cm. What is its volume? (π = 3.14, to 2 decimal places)
Why does Greenland look so large on many world maps?
qa.a: The Mercator projection, a cylindrical map, stretches regions near the poles
qa.e: Areas far from the equator get enlarged in such projections.

qa.q: A ball's radius is doubled. How many times larger is its surface area?
qa.e: Area scales by k² = 4.

qa.q: A balloon's radius increases by 10%. By what percentage does its volume increase?
A balloon's radius increases by 50%. Its surface area becomes how many times as large?
The inner surface of a hemispherical bowl of radius 14 cm is to be polished at ₹0.50 per cm². What is the cost? (π = 22/7)
A hemispherical shell has outer radius 7 cm and inner radius 3.5 cm. What is the volume of material? (π = 22/7)
A solid hemisphere has radius 7 cm. What is its total surface area? (π = 22/7)
The volume of a sphere becomes 27 times as large. What happened to its radius?
qa.e: k³ = 27 gives k = 3.

qa.q: A cuboid water bottle crate is 40 cm × 30 cm × 25 cm. How many litres is that?
How many cm² are in 3.5 m²?
A drum holds 0.2 m³. How many litres is that?
What is the first step of a good guesstimate?
qa.e: Assumptions make the estimate clear and checkable.

qa.q: Two students estimate tennis balls in a classroom: one gets 30,000 and the other 60,000. Why can both be sensible?
qa.a: They made different assumptions about room size or packing
qa.e: Guesstimates depend on assumptions; state them clearly.

qa.q: A golgappa stall sells about 300 plates a day, 6 golgappas a plate. Roughly how many golgappas in 30 days?
Estimate the volume of a classroom 8 m × 6 m × 3 m in litres.
A ball-pen refill is a thin cylinder of radius 0.1 cm and length 10 cm. Roughly how much ink can it hold? (π ≈ 3)
A string around a ball of radius R is lengthened by 2π metres. By how much does the gap grow?
qa.e: 2π = 2π × gap, so gap = 1 m.

qa.q: A string around the equator is lengthened by 1 m. About how high above the ground is it now? (π = 3.14)
Does the gap in the Earth-string puzzle depend on the Earth's radius?
qa.a: No, it is always 1/(2π) m for 1 m of extra string
qa.e: The R terms cancel: 2π(R + g) − 2πR = 2πg.

qa.q: A cube has volume 216 cm³. What is its surface area?
A cube has surface area 384 cm². What is its volume?
Using S = 6V^(2/3), what is S for V = 343?
A cube's volume is multiplied by 8. Its surface area is multiplied by:
qa.e: Edge × 2, so area × 4.

qa.q: A string is tight around a pole of radius 10 cm. To make a gap of 5 cm all round, how much extra string is needed? (π = 3.14)
qa.e: Extra = 2π × 5.
